implementation_strategy: Execute confirmatory paired design using a hosted LLM API (openai_responses:gpt-5-mini) under a Docker-based deterministic validation pipeline. For each of 200 tasks: (1) single deterministic initial generation call (temperature=0) shared across both conditions; (2) baseline condition: record primary deterministic validator (Batfish) verdict on initial candidate; (3) guarded condition: run the same initial candidate through Batfish; if Batfish reports violations, issue at most one automated repair prompt to gpt-5-mini (per adapter-enforced cap) then re-run Batfish; (4) archive model-call logs, validator traces, canonicalized configs, hashes, and flags. Secondary emulator (Mininet) audit executed deterministically on a fixed 10% holdout (20 tasks) in Docker. All scoring, flagging, exclusion, and sensitivity handling performed by deterministic code and the registered analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). No human annotation, adjudication, or manual scoring is used.
public_resources: Curated public/synthetic NetOps task bank v1 (200 confirmatory tasks; 4 topology clusters × 50 tasks)
task_manifest_strategy: Use the curated public/synthetic NetOps task bank v1. Stratify by topology cluster (enterprise, campus, datacenter, edge) with 50 tasks per cluster. Tasks canonicalized to machine-checkable intent representations. Task ordering randomized with fixed seed for execution.
transformation_manifest_strategy: Baseline transformation: direct_configuration_generation_v1 (one deterministic generation per task). Guarded transformation: generate_validate_repair_v1 (shared initial candidate; Batfish validation; if fail issue up to one repair prompt; re-validate). Syntactic canonicalization and semantic parsing applied deterministically to all generated configs before validation.
randomisation_plan: Randomize task execution order with fixed PRNG seed 42. Within each batch, task order is the randomized order derived from seed 42.
caching_plan: Cache all initial generation outputs, repair responses, Batfish validator outputs, and Mininet traces to local storage. Reuse cached artifacts for deterministic re-analysis and to avoid additional model calls. Model calls are not repeated unless required by infrastructure retry procedures; no caching bypass that would generate extra model calls is performed.
failure_recovery_plan: No human intervention. If an infrastructure failure prevents completion of a pair, handle deterministically per missingness_plan: pairs where neither condition completes are excluded from primary analysis and logged. No additional LLM calls beyond per-task caps. Infrastructure-only retries (e.g., transient API/network errors) limited to controller restarts that do not consume additional model-call budget; any such retry attempts and outcomes are logged. Discrepancies Batfish vs Mininet are flagged automatically and handled per contamination_plan.
result_schema: paired_binary_episode_v1 (v1.0): per-task record contains task_id, intent canonical form, initial_candidate_text, initial_candidate_canonical, baseline_validator_verdict (Batfish), guarded_validator_sequence (pre-repair verdicts, repair_prompt_text if any, repair_response_text, post-repair verdict), final_pass_fail_flags for both conditions, repair_iterations_count, Batfish diagnostics, Mininet_emulator_trace (for audited holdout), discrepancy_flags, exclusion_flag, hashes, timestamps, and model-call metadata.
estimated_compute_notes: Totals derived: confirmatory sample n=200 => initial generation calls = 200 (one deterministic call per task). Expected repair calls estimated ≈100 (empirically expected avg ≈0.5 repairs/task), yielding estimated_model_calls = 200 + 100 = 300. Adapter-enforced worst-case maximum_model_calls = 200 initial + 200 possible repairs = 400. All values within global capability cap (maximum_planned_model_calls=10000).
